scorecards.analysisText:
Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as FY results accordingly. Next year end = 31/12/25 → FY1 = FY25 · prior year = FY24 · FY2 = FY26. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Year label mappings (derived from Next year end = 31/12/25):

  • FY1 = FY25 (1y fc in Sharescope)
  • FY1−1 = FY24 (1y ago in Sharescope)
  • FY1−2 = FY23 (2y ago in Sharescope)
  • FY1−3 = FY22 (3y ago in Sharescope)
  • FY2 = FY26 (2y fc in Sharescope)

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

JTC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

  • Routing: pre-FY mode (Q2). Incoming RNS = FY25 full year results.
  • FY1 consensus (FY25e): EPS 49.7p · Revenue £385.1m
  • FY2 consensus (FY26e): EPS 60.4p · Revenue £454.8m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change −0.2p (−0.2%) over full snapshot period. Last-4-week trend: 🟡 STALLING (flat at 49.7p since 13 Mar 26). Revenue net change: £385.1m vs £387.3m at earliest snapshot = −£2.2m (−0.6%). No net upgrades visible in the snapshot window — consensus has drifted marginally lower.
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 47.3% of FY = £182.2m · EPS 46.5% of FY = 23.1p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY24): Revenue £147.1m · EPS 19.9p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode, RNS-derived): FY25 actual £381.9m − H1 actual £172.6m = implied H2 Rev £209.3m vs prior H2 £158.3m → +32.2% YoY. FY25 EPS 45.55p − H1 actual 21.3p = implied H2 EPS 24.25p vs prior H2 27.5p → −11.8% YoY.
  • FX: Revenue growth on constant currency basis 26.7% vs reported 25.1% — difference = 1.6pp, exceeding 0.5pp threshold. USD is material exposure (~32% of revenue). Phase 0B triggered — assessed below.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt (underlying): FY23 £13.9m → FY24 £182.3m → FY25 £275.8m (actual) → FY26fc £232.3m · ND/EBITDA: FY23 3.2x / FY24 1.9x (underlying) / FY25 2.22x (actual) / FY26fc 1.6x · Interest cover FY25 actual: 0.9x (reported) / 3.9x (fc — note fc was pre-RNS) · ND/FCF FY25fc: 3.4x · Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — 2.22x underlying EBITDA, above 1.5–2.0x guidance but anticipated; annualised acquisitions bring within range. Interest cover on underlying basis adequate; reported cover distorted by EIP/non-underlying items.

Phase 0B assessment: USD ~32% of revenue. Constant currency growth 26.7% vs reported 25.1% = 1.6pp difference — GBP strengthening created a headwind. 1.6pp exceeds 0.5pp threshold so override does not fire. However, exposure is 30–35% band and impact is modest (1.6pp on revenue). Applying mid-point of 30–35% headwind band: 🔴 GBP headwind — FX Rule 1 applied (−4 pts mid-point of −4 band for modest headwind). Badge: FX Rule 1 applied (−4 pts) · ~32% USD · GBP headwind.

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

JTC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

RNS type: Full Year Results

1. Revenue — FY25 actual FY25 revenue: £381.9m (+25.1% YoY vs FY24 £305.4m). Vs FY25e consensus £385.1m = miss of £3.2m (−0.8%). Inorganic contributed £55.1m (Citi Trust, KHT). Organic growth 8.5% (vs 11.3% in FY24). Constant currency growth 26.7%.

"Revenue grew 25.1% to £381.9m (2024: £305.4m) and underlying EBITDA increased 22.4% to £124.5m (2024: £101.7m). Net organic growth was 8.5% (2024: 11.3%)."

Implied H2 revenue: £381.9m − £172.6m = £209.3m vs prior H2 £158.3m (+32.2% YoY) — strong, driven by Citi Trust H2 contribution (acquired 1 Jul 2025, contributed £32.8m inorganic in period).

2. EPS / earnings — FY25 actual Underlying basic EPS: 45.55p (+9.0% YoY vs FY24 41.80p). Vs FY25e consensus 49.7p = miss of 4.15p (−8.3%). Reported basic EPS 0.56p (2024: −4.44p). The EPS miss vs consensus is material.

"Underlying basic EPS (a / b): 45.55p (2024: 41.80p). The growth in underlying EPS of 9.0% was relatively lower than EBITDA growth of 22.4%. This was driven by the increased interest expense on our borrowings that fund M&A activity (with only a 6 month contribution from Citi and 2 months from KHT), and the increased volume of shares in the period."

EPS quality check: Effective tax rate on underlying profit = £7.4m tax on £8.4m PBT (reported) = 88.8% — but this is heavily distorted by non-underlying items. On underlying basis: tax charge not separately broken out cleanly, but the CFO notes effective tax rate 5.8% on underlying basis (2024: 4.9%). 5.8% is low but consistent with Jersey domicile. No material deviation from prior year normalised rate. No tax-distorted beat — the miss is genuine. 🚨 Note: acquisition dilution (interest step-up from £184.2m drawdowns, share count increase from Galaxy EIP award exercise) compressed the EPS bridge materially.

FY26e EPS bridge (constructed here, referenced in Phase 4 #2):

  • New base: FY25 underlying EPS 45.55p (168.0m shares)
  • Inorganic annualisation delta: Citi Trust contributed 6 months (H2 only) in FY25 — full annualisation in FY26 adds ~£32.8m × 2 − £32.8m = +£32.8m incremental revenue; at 32.6% EBITDA margin = ~+£10.7m EBITDA. KHT contributed 2 months — full year adds ~£14.5m revenue at ~37% margin = ~+£5.4m EBITDA. Combined annualisation EBITDA uplift ~£16.1m.
  • Organic EBITDA growth delta: disclosed organic growth 8.5% — applying to FY25 organic revenue base ~£321m × 8.5% × 32.6% margin ≈ +£8.9m EBITDA organic contribution.
  • Interest step-up delta: FY25 bank loan interest £21.6m on average drawn debt. FY26 will see full-year cost of £184.2m net drawdowns at SONIA+ margin + US PP notes at 6.25%. Estimated FY26 interest: ~£28–30m (vs FY25 £21.6m) = incremental ~£6–8m interest headwind vs FY25 actuals.
  • Net EBITDA uplift (annualisation + organic): ~+£25m; minus additional D&A on acquired intangibles (~£5m uplift from full-year Citi/KHT); minus interest step-up ~£7m; minus tax at ~7% effective = net underlying profit uplift ~£11–13m.
  • Implied FY26 underlying profit: £76.5m + £11–13m = ~£87.5–89.5m. At 168m shares = ~52–53p EPS.
  • Stale FY26 consensus: 60.4p. Implied shortfall vs consensus: −7.4 to −8.4p (−12 to −14%).
  • This strongly suggests FY26 consensus needs to come down. The stale consensus appears to have assumed either higher organic growth or lower interest costs than actuals now imply.

3. Order book / forward work New business wins record: £43.5m (+21.8% vs FY24 £35.7m). Revenue retention 98.6% (FY24: 98.4%). Pipeline described as "healthy". No specific order book figure disclosed.

"We had another record year of new business wins totalling £43.5m at the period end (2024: £35.7m). The new business pipeline remains healthy."

4. Margin, profitability, costs Underlying EBITDA: £124.5m (+22.4% YoY). Underlying EBITDA margin 32.6% (FY24: 33.3%) — down 0.7pp. Management's medium-term guidance range: 33–38%. FY25 margin is below the bottom of the guidance range. ICS margin 28.8% (FY24: 30.6%) — deterioration flagged as investment-driven plus regulatory headwind on chargeable time. PCS margin 37.3% (FY24: 37.3%) — flat, showing Citi Trust integration delivered at JTC margins. Finance costs up 34.0% YoY (£31.2m vs £25.4m), driven by £184.2m debt drawdowns.

"Our underlying EBITDA margin reported a drop to 32.6% (2024: 33.3%). 2025 continued to be a year of market volatility, with the impact being most prominent in the ICS division."

Forward-looking margin guidance: nil explicit numeric. Management commentary references continued investment in infrastructure and regulatory compliance. No guidance for FY26 margin improvement stated.

5. Capital returns and balance sheet Dividend: 5p total for FY25 (FY24: 12.54p). Cut of 60.1% — driven entirely by the pending Permira acquisition. No final dividend declared due to offer period. This is a one-off structural event, not a going-concern signal.

Net debt (underlying) at FY25 year-end: £275.8m (vs FY24: £182.3m). Underlying ND/EBITDA: 2.22x (vs guidance 1.5–2.0x, above range as expected post-M&A). Undrawn facilities: £27.4m of £400m bank + $100m of $175m US PP.

"Our underlying net debt/underlying EBITDA leverage at the period end was 2.22x (2024: 1.79x), above our guidance range (1.5x - 2.0x). This increase was expected, with the period seeing increased M&A activity."

6. Qualitative tone / acquisition context Permira acquisition: agreed at £13.40/share (Nov 2025). Shareholder approval received Jan 2026. Expected to complete Q3 2026. This is the dominant structural overlay — the company is in an offer period, no earnings guidance can be given, no broker presentations held.

"Based on current expectations, the transaction is expected to complete during the third quarter of 2026, subject to satisfaction of the remaining conditions."

7. Constant currency / FX Constant currency revenue growth 26.7% vs reported 25.1% — 1.6pp drag from GBP strengthening vs USD.

B. Outlook & Guidance Classification

JTC is in an active offer period (Permira £13.40 cash bid). No FY26 guidance is given — legally restricted from doing so. The RNS closes the Cosmos era and introduces "Genesis" under private ownership. No earnings trajectory stated for FY26. No "comfortable with" language. No "ahead of expectations" language.

Classification: 🟡 In-line for outlook — but this is structurally constrained by the offer period. There is no positive upgrade signal and no downgrade warning beyond the mechanical miss on FY25 EPS vs consensus.

Exact guidance phrase: none — offer period restriction. Guidance: nil (qualitative only — "resilient", "record wins", "healthy pipeline"). Covers: not applicable. Provisional points: 0 to +3 (In-line, upper end given record new wins and healthy pipeline language, but nil numeric guidance caps this).

Divergence check: FY25 EPS missed consensus by 8.3%, yet qualitative language is constructive ("resilient performance", "record new business wins"). Current year miss + constructive qualitative tone = divergence. Carry as: 🟡 Beat quality — forward guidance diverges from current year delivery (EPS missed consensus materially; qualitative tone does not reflect this adequately).

PHASE 3 — HISTORICAL BENCHMARKING

JTC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

3a. Full-Year YoY Growth Table

*FY26e = stale pre-RNS consensus. EPS bridge in Phase 2 implies FY26e needs to reset to ~52–53p.

Revenue growth trajectory: 🟢 Accelerating — three most recent YoY: +18.6% (FY24) → +25.1% (FY25) → implied +19.1% (FY26 consensus, though this will be revised). FY25 reaccelerated materially vs FY24, driven by Citi Trust acquisition.

EPS growth trajectory: 🔴 Decelerating — +12.0% (FY23) → +12.1% (FY24) → +9.0% (FY25). Three consecutive years of growth but rate compressing, driven by interest cost step-up and dilution from acquired shares.

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: RNS-derived FY25 +25.1% vs prior year (FY24) +18.6% → acceleration ✓ (RNS-derived)
  • EPS: RNS-derived FY25 +9.0% vs prior year (FY24) +12.1% → no acceleration — deceleration (RNS-derived)

3.1 Half-on-Half (HoH) Growth Pattern

H2 cross-check:

  • FY23: H1 93.0 + H2 107.0 = 200.0 ✓
  • FY24: H1 121.5 + H2 135.9 = 257.4 ✓
  • FY24 EPS: H1 18.2 + H2 19.1 = 37.3 ✓
  • FY25 EPS H2: Sharescope H2 field = blank (−). FY25 actual 45.55p − H1 21.3p = 24.25p (RNS-derived). Note: Sharescope H1 EPS shown as 21.3p — this is the current H1 field.
  • FY24 H2 EBITDA: Sharescope shows 1y ago H2 = −49.1 (corrupt — negative EBITDA impossible). ⚠️ FY24 EBITDA H2 field corrupt in Sharescope. Ignored; not needed for scoring.
  • FY25 Revenue H2: £381.9m − £172.6m = £209.3m (RNS-derived).
  • FY24 Revenue H2: Sharescope 1y ago H2 = £158.3m. Cross-check: £147.1m + £158.3m = £305.4m ✓

Revenue trajectory (HoH): 🟢 Accelerating — three most recent HoH YoY: H1 +17.3% → H2 +32.2%. H2 surge driven entirely by Citi Trust acquisition (6-month contribution). Underlying organic H2 would be more modest.

EPS trajectory (HoH): 🔴 Decelerating — H2 FY24 +44.0% (Galaxy EIP share award exercise distorted EPS comparison — FY24 H2 EPS 27.5p was inflated by timing of EIP-related share count reduction); H1 FY25 +7.0%; H2 FY25 −11.8%. H2 EPS decline reflects interest cost step-up post-acquisitions fully biting in H2 with only 6-month Citi contribution to EBITDA but full-year debt cost in H1 for earlier drawdowns plus H2 drawdowns.

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline (pre-H1 mode only)

Mode = pre-FY (Q2) → Phase 3.2 written in full but does not contribute a scored row to Phase 5.

Baseline:

  • Revenue: 47.3% × £385.1m = £182.2m
  • EPS: 46.5% × 49.7p = 23.1p

H1 FY25 actuals are available from Sharescope current H1 field (£172.6m revenue, 21.3p EPS) — these are balance of year actuals embedded in the data. However, the data source gate requires RNS-disclosed figures. The RNS does not explicitly state H1 figures as a disclosed line item; the FY RNS provides only full-year numbers. The H1 result was separately reported earlier in the year. Sharescope current H1 figures used here are historic actuals from the H1 reporting date — not RNS-sourced from this document.

Tracking deviation (informational only — pre-FY mode, not scored):

  • Revenue: £172.6m ÷ £385.1m = 44.8% vs baseline 47.3% → deviation 🔴 [−2.5pp]
  • EPS: 21.3p ÷ 49.7p = 42.9% vs baseline 46.5% → deviation 🔴 [−3.6pp]

These signals are informational given we now have FY actuals. They confirm that JTC tracked below its seasonal baseline in H1, with H2 acquisition-driven catch-up partially restoring revenue but not EPS.

H2 EPS burden: FY1 consensus 49.7p − H1 actual 21.3p = 28.4p required vs historical H2 avg ~21.2p [(17.1+19.1+27.5)/3]. Burden was HIGHER than historical average — and FY25 actual H2 EPS of 24.25p fell below both the burden implied by consensus (28.4p) and the prior H2 (27.5p).

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode — scored)

H2 base: RNS-derived. FY25 actual £381.9m / 45.55p. H1 actuals from prior reporting.

H2 Revenue: £209.3m vs prior H2 £158.3m → +32.2% YoY → 🟢 strong (>+10%) H2 EPS: 24.25p vs prior H2 27.5p → −11.8% YoY → 🔴 weak (−5 to −15%)

Revenue H2 strength is acquisition-driven (Citi Trust 6 months). Organic H2 revenue would strip out ~£32.8m inorganic → organic H2 ~£176.5m vs £158.3m = +11.5% — still strong organically.

EPS H2 weakness is structural: interest step-up (£184.2m drawdowns in FY25), share count marginally higher, partial EBITDA contribution from acquisitions (only H2 for Citi, only 2 months for KHT) vs full-year interest cost on drawdowns.

Revenue H2: 🟢 strong (RNS-derived) EPS H2: 🔴 weak (RNS-derived)

Profit warning feasibility gate (pre-H1 mode only): Not applicable — mode = pre-FY.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

EPS trend: −0.2p (−0.2%) net change over full period (49.8p → 49.7p). Marginal drift lower — no upgrade cycle visible. Zero meaningful revision events in the 46-week snapshot window. 4-week trend: 🟡 STEADY/FLAT (no movement since 13 Mar 26).

Revenue trend: £387.3m → £385.1m = −£2.2m (−0.6%) net change. Mild drift lower in line with EPS.

Divergence: Price has risen from £12.43 to £13.00 over the period while forecasts have drifted very marginally lower. Price action entirely explained by the Permira offer at £13.40 (announced Nov 2025) — the price is trading at a discount to the offer, with spread reflecting regulatory/timing risk. Broker forecasts are effectively redundant as price anchors to the offer price.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP.

  • Net debt (underlying): FY22 ~n/a / FY23 £13.9m / FY24 £182.3m / FY25 H1 £276.5m / FY25 actual £275.8m / FY26fc £232.3m
  • ND/EBITDA: FY22 3.2x / FY23 n/a / FY24 1.9x (underlying) / FY25 2.22x (actual) / FY26fc 1.6x
  • Interest cover: FY25 actual reported 0.9x (distorted by non-underlying); underlying basis ~3.9x (pre-RNS fc) — actual underlying cover close to 3.9x given EBITDA £124.5m and finance cost (ex-unwinding NPV discounts) ~£22.5m = ~5.5x on EBITDA basis. FY26fc: 4.9x.
  • ND/FCF: FY25fc 3.4x / FY26fc 2.4x

Debt flag: 🟡 Manageable leverage — 2.22x ND/EBITDA, above 1.5–2.0x guidance but explicitly anticipated and expected to revert to range when annualising acquisitions. Interest cover adequate. Covenant risk low given undrawn facilities. No Phase 5 scored row.

Forecast year earnings check:

Step 1 — FY25 vs FY24 actual:

  • FY25 actual EPS 45.55p vs FY24 actual 41.80p → ✅ growing (+9.0%)
  • FY25 actual Revenue £381.9m vs FY24 actual £305.4m → ✅ growing (+25.1%)
  • ✅✅ FY25 EPS and Revenue both growing vs prior year actual.

Step 2 — FY26 fc vs FY25 actual:

  • FY26fc EPS 60.4p vs FY25 actual 45.55p → ✅ growing (+32.6%) — but EPS bridge implies 60.4p is materially overstated; realistic FY26 EPS ~52–53p.
  • FY26fc Revenue £454.8m vs FY25 actual £381.9m → ✅ growing (+19.1%)
  • ✅✅ FY26fc EPS and Revenue both growing vs FY25 actual on stale consensus. However: 🚨 FY26 consensus EPS 60.4p likely overstated by ~8–10p vs implied bridge (~52–53p) — stale consensus pre-acquisition annualisation maths and pre-interest-step-up.

3.6 Structural flags

Permira acquisition overlay: JTC is subject to a recommended cash offer at £13.40/share. Expected Q3 2026 completion. This makes FY26 broker forecasts largely irrelevant for investment purposes — the instrument will be delisted. Any broker revisions post-RNS are mechanical exercises only. The offer price is the terminal value.

"Based on current expectations, the transaction is expected to complete during the third quarter of 2026, subject to satisfaction of the remaining conditions."

Organic growth deceleration: 8.5% (FY25) vs 11.3% (FY24) — rolling 3yr avg 13.2%. Management acknowledges macro headwinds (fund launch delays, interest rate headwind to Banking/Treasury services). Medium-term guidance 10%+ — FY25 is below this.

"The subdued organic growth for the year was a result of macroeconomic conditions, albeit strong in the context of our overall market."

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

JTC · Q2 · Full Year Results · FY25 · Year end: 31/12/25

#1 Driver — EPS miss vs consensus The dominant #1 driver is the EPS shortfall of 4.15p (−8.3%) vs FY25e consensus of 49.7p. Underlying EPS 45.55p is below the entire consensus range. Interest step-up from £184.2m net drawdowns and partial acquisition contribution are the mechanical causes. Brokers will need to cut FY25 actuals through their models and reassess FY26 from this lower base. This is the single metric that drives all revision activity.

#2 Driver — FY26 EPS consensus reset The #2 driver is the implied FY26 consensus reset. Stale consensus at 60.4p was built on assumptions that pre-dated the Citi Trust acquisition's full P&L impact (higher interest, partial EBITDA). The EPS bridge (Phase 2) implies ~52–53p as the realistic FY26 level — a ~−12 to −14% cut required. Revenue consensus (£454.8m) is more defensible given annualisation of Citi/KHT, but EPS leverage is the crux.

#2 Forecast revisions (FY25 and FY26):

  • FY25 EPS: actual 45.55p vs 49.7p consensus — no revision needed, actuals published. Models reset to 45.55p base.
  • FY26 EPS: expected revision down to ~52–53p from 60.4p = approximately −12 to −14%. Direction: cut.
  • FY25 Revenue: actual £381.9m vs £385.1m consensus = −0.8% miss. Minor.
  • FY26 Revenue: likely modest cut from £454.8m toward ~£440–450m reflecting lower organic growth trajectory and FX headwind. Direction: modest cut, −1 to −3%.
  • FY26 EPS revision direction: cut. Net FY1 (now FY26) EPS revision: cut.

#3 Target price and recommendation: Consensus TP is £13.00 — irrelevant. The Permira offer at £13.40 is the effective ceiling and floor for the share price. Brokers will formally mark TPs to the offer price (£13.40) or close to it. Recommendations will shift to "accept offer" / tender. No traditional upgrade/downgrade dynamic applies. Current price £13.04 implies a 2.8% discount to offer — spread reflects regulatory completion risk (Q3 2026).

#4 Conservative guidance read-through: No guidance language at all — offer period restriction. No "not less than" language. No "comfortable with" language. There is no upgrade cycle probability — the company is being acquired. This is the terminal RNS.

#5 Key risk: The single largest risk is regulatory delay or deal failure. If Permira's acquisition does not complete (regulatory rejection, competing bid, JTC break-up), the share would reprice sharply lower toward fundamental value — which on a 45.55p EPS base and pre-offer multiple would be well below £13.40. Additionally, ongoing organic growth deceleration (8.5% vs 10%+ target) and ICS margin compression (28.8% vs 30.6%) represent structural concerns if the deal were to fall away.

"All necessary regulatory consents and required completion approvals are now being sought and the process continues to move forward positively."

Consistency check: Net FY26 EPS revision direction = cut (−12 to −14%). Tone must be: Cautious or Negative.
